_comment: Inputs for /january-paycheck-change-calculator/ that live nowhere else. The 2027 federal figures are NOT here: they come from projections-2027.json (official2027 once the IRS Revenue Procedure is in, the publishers' thirdPartyProjections until then) or from tax-data-2027.json once that file exists, which also replaces every state below. The 2027 Social Security wage base comes from projections-2027.json ssaFactSheet2027.

stateOverrides2027._rule: Only a 2027 figure already set in statute AND already recorded in this repo goes here, patched over the state's 2026 `tax` block for the January paycheck. Everything else uses the 2026 tables, and the page says so. North Carolina added 2026-11-03: S.B. 257 (the 2026 Appropriations Act) is Session Law 2026-41 (ncleg summary title 'S257 - 2026 Appropriations Act. (SL 2026-41)'), already cited in state-payroll-2026.json.

virginia.label: Virginia's 2027 standard deduction
virginia.what: Virginia's standard deduction goes up in 2027, to $9,200 for a single filer and $18,400 for a married couple, under state law. Its $930 personal exemption does not change.
virginia._math: The engine's Virginia standardDeduction field carries the standard deduction plus the personal exemption (see the virginia _source in tax-data-2026.json, 'PERSONAL EXEMPTION FOLDED IN 2026-10-03'): 9,200 + 930 = 10,130 single and head of household; 18,400 + 2 x 930 = 20,260 married filing jointly.
virginia._quote: Va. Code 58.1-322.03(1)(b), currency 8/1/2026: '(vi) for taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2027, but before January 1, 2028, $9,200 for single individuals and $18,400 for married persons'. Recorded in tax-data-2026.json virginia _watch and _source.

north-carolina.label: North Carolina's 2027 income tax rate
north-carolina.what: North Carolina's flat income tax rate drops from 3.99% to 3.49% in 2027 under state law, so a little less state tax comes out of each check.
north-carolina._quote: S.L. 2026-41 (S.B. 257, 2026 Appropriations Act, signed 2026-07-07): 3.49% for taxable years 2027-2029, triggers repealed (EY Tax News 2026-1630; ncleg summary S257-SMSA-88(sl)). NCDOR: 3.99% for taxable years after 2025.
